turn: I added syntax highlighting for fenced code blocks in the Markdown pipeline. The new `src/markdown/highlight.js` uses highlight.js. It uses the language named on the fence when highlight.js recognizes it, and otherwise falls back to auto-detection. I haven't run the code or any tests in this session, so none of this has been checked by running it. All I did was read the module to confirm the fallback logic. In the same commit I made one small unplanned fix. I stopped the pipeline from treating an empty info string on a fence as a language name, so a bare fence now takes the auto-detect path instead of a failed lookup. Next I'll start on "Sidebar navigation from folders".

sidefix.title: Handle empty fence info strings
sidefix.what: Code fences with an empty info string are no longer treated as a language name, so they fall back to auto-detection.
